create.name: Añjanauka
create.about: Śrī Viśākhā Sakhī's place of residence. Here Kṛṣṇa applied kajala (añjana) to Śrīmatī Rādhikā's eyes: She had come to meet Him at the sound of His flute before the añjana was put on. Kiśorī-kuṇḍa lies to the south of the village; on its west bank is the añjanī-śilā on which Kṛṣṇa seated Rādhā to decorate Her eyes. There is also a rāsa-maṇḍala.

create.name: Caraṇa-pahāḍī (Choṭī-baiṭhana)
create.about: Hill with the footprints (caraṇa-cihna) of Śrī Kṛṣṇa and Baladeva, and imprints of cows and gopas. Standing on top of the hill, Kṛṣṇa played His flute in His threefold-bending form; the whole hill melted at the sound, and the cowherd boys, cows, deer and other animals hurrying towards Him left their imprints in the stones, all pointing in one direction. Nearby is Caraṇa-gaṅgā.

create.name: Khelanvana (Śergaḍh)
create.about: Where Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma played (khelna) many games with the sakhās while herding the cows, and Śrīmatī Rādhikā played with Her sakhīs. Nanda Bābā and Vṛṣabhānu Bābā stayed here for some time with their families and cows.

create.name: Vihāravana
create.about: Where Vraja-bihārī Kṛṣṇa with Rādhikā and the gopīs performed rāsa and other pastimes near the Yamunā. Darśana of the Bihārījī temple and Vihāra-kuṇḍa. The forest is still somewhat protected: cuckoos sing, thousands of peacocks dance in the rainy season, and there are many kuñjas, kadamba groves and creepers.

create.name: Muñjāṭavī
create.about: The muñja-grass forest where the cows, and then the sakhās looking for them, were lost in the summer heat; Kaṁsa's followers set it on fire, and when the boys cried out, Kṛṣṇa told them to close their eyes and swallowed the forest fire.

create.name: Bandī-Ānandī
create.location: A short distance south of Lohavana
create.about: Bandī and Ānandī were two heavenly devīs who, on the excuse of making cow-dung patties at Nanda Bābā's place, came to have Kṛṣṇa's darśana. Their kuṇḍas are still here in their memory.

create.name: Garuḍa-Govinda
create.about: While grazing the cows, Kṛṣṇa made Śrīdāma Sakhā take the role of Garuḍa and climbed on his back, as if He were Nārāyaṇa. Even today one can have darśana of Govindajī with Śrīdāma as Garuḍa.
